summary: Gérard Colas is an indologist. He served as Directeur de recherche at the CNRS (attested in 2004 and at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2012) and as a Senior Fellow at the CNRS (attested 2009).
Gérard Cotton worked in indology and linguistics. He studied under Joseph Mansion and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Liège by 1930.

Gérard Devèze was an indologist and linguist. He earned a diploma in Tamil under Julien Vinson at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales by 1885, and also earned a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Gérard Fussman specialized in indology, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure (~1960–1964), he succeeded Jean Filliozat as professor at the Collège de France in 1984 and headed a CNRS unit (attested 1994).

Gérard Huet works in computational science, indology, and linguistics. He studied under George Ernst (~1970–1972) and Maurice Nivat (~1972–1976), and served as a professor at Inria from ~1974 to 2017.

Géza Bethlenfalvy was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under János Harmatta and Lajos Ligeti. His career included posts at the University of Delhi (1970), Vienna (2007–2008), and Eötvös Loránd University.

Géza Uray was a Tibetologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Lajos Ligeti in 1942. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (1948–1949; 1979), the Research Centre for Linguistics (~1951–1973), and the University of Pennsylvania (1973–1984).

Gösta Liebert was an indologist and linguist who studied at Gothenburg and Lund under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He taught at Lund (1949–1955), Uppsala (1951–1953), and served as professor at Gothenburg (1955–1982).

Götz von Selle was a historian and Central Asianist who earned his Dr. phil. at Göttingen (~1914–1920). He worked as a librarian at Göttingen and Berlin, and became honorary professor and library director at the University of Königsberg in 1939.
Günter Blamberger held posts at the University of Kassel (~1989–1993) and served as Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne from ~1993 to 2020.

Günter Grönbold specializes in indology, tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctorate under Helmut Hoffmann (~1964–1969) and worked at the Bavarian State Library from ~1974 to 2008, where he headed the Oriental Section (~1988–2008).

Günter Lanczkowski was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, completing his PhD at Marburg in 1947. He served as Privatdocent at Heidelberg (1960–1982) and later taught religion at Mainz (1984–1986) and Munich (1986–1988).

Günter Schweiger is a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the Vienna University of Economics and Business and under Gert Klingenschmitt, he was a professor at WU Vienna (1974–2009) and held several visiting professorships.

Günther Schulemann worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Berlin, Freiburg, and Breslau (Ph.D. ~1911–1913), later serving as Privatdozent (1923) and professor of philosophy (1930–1939) at the University of Breslau.

Günther Weibgen was an indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He served at the Royal Library of Berlin, succeeding Johannes Nobel in 1928 and becoming Oberbibliothekar in 1944.

Günther-Dietz Sontheimer was an indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tübingen, ILS Law College, and SOAS under scholars including Helmuth von Glasenapp and J. Duncan M. Derrett, later serving as professor at Heidelberg University from 1965 to 1992.

H. Craig Melchert is a linguist who studied at Michigan State, the Defense Language Institute, the National Cryptologic School, and Harvard. He held academic posts at UNC Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and UCLA (2007–2015).

H. G. Narahari was an indologist who studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he held posts at the Adyar Library and Research Centre and the University of Madras.
H. J. de Graaf was a historian who studied at Leiden University (~1919–1935) and under Poerbatjaraka (1927–1930).
H. Kikuchi pursued Buddhist studies and Indology, studying as a research student at the University of Delhi under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale (attested 1966).
